Assemble multiple RTF files into one

Source: R/assemble_rtf.R
assemble_rtf.Rd

assemble_rtf() concatenates several RTF files generated by generate_rtfreport() into a single deliverable. Each input file becomes one or more sections of the assembled output; the document header (font / colour tables, page settings) is taken from the first input.

Usage

assemble_rtf(
  input_files = NULL,
  output_file,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  cover = NULL,
  toc = NULL,
  toc_title = "Table of Contents",
  toc_leader = c("dot", "none"),
  bookmark_prefix = "tfl_",
  book_page = NULL,
  toc_style = getOption("rtfreporter.toc_style")
)

Arguments

input_files

Character vector of paths to RTF files to combine (at least 2). May be left out when toc is a table (or its path): the table's file column, in its order.

output_file

Path for the assembled output RTF file: a single string, in a folder that exists, and not one of the input_files.

overwrite

TRUE or FALSE; whether to overwrite an existing output file. Default FALSE.

cover

Optional list(title, subtitle, date, version, meta) for a cover page. NULL (default) = no cover page.

toc

Table-of-Contents specification. NULL (default) = no TOC, no bookmarks; "auto" = auto-extract titles; a character vector = one label per input file; a table (column file, and optionally label, heading, level) or the path of one (.xlsx / .csv) = multi-level layout. See Table of Contents above.

toc_title

Bold title rendered on the TOC page, a single string ("" = an empty title line). Named l, c or r as a header cell is, it is aligned left, centre or right (c(l = "Contents")); unnamed it is centred. "\n" is a line break in the title, and the tokens of rtf_text_tokens() that need no page are filled as in a title: the session's own tokens (options(rtfreporter.tokens = )), {DATETIME}, {PROGRAM}. A token that is none of them stays as text. The same goes for the text of a heading of a table toc. Default "Table of Contents".

toc_leader

"dot" (default) draws a dotted leader between each TOC entry and its page number; "none" leaves whitespace.

bookmark_prefix

String prepended to every auto-generated bookmark name (default "tfl_"): letters, digits and _ only, as a bookmark name allows; "" = none. Helps avoid clashes if you later concatenate multiple assembled outputs.

book_page

Text for the compiled document's page number, a single string put into every {BOOK_PAGE} slot the inputs reserved. NULL (default) leaves the slots empty.

Why a slot

A deliverable that will be bound into a book needs two page numbers: its own (Page 1 of 3) and the book's (Page 4 of 57). Written from the start they print the same number twice on a standalone deliverable, where the two are equal. So the deliverable reserves the position instead – c(c = "{BOOK_PAGE}") in whichever band it wants, header, footer, title or footnote – and renders it empty, keeping the row's height. This argument supplies the content when the book is built, so filling it cannot shift anything.

What to give

Typically "Page {AUTO_PAGE} of {AUTO_TOTAL_PAGES}". The total resolves to the book's page count, which is what the deliverable could not know on its own. Both follow Page numbering above: the page is counted from the book's first page, a cover and the table of contents included, and the total is all of its pages (the first table after a cover and a one-page table of contents of a 9-page book reads Page 3 of 9).

Refused

The static {PAGE} / {TOTAL_PAGES} are rejected: the slot sits in one band shared by every page of a section, so a single substitution cannot give each page its own number.

toc_style

The size and boldness of the TOC's text: NULL (the built-in sizes) or a list with the keys title, heading and entry, each list(size = <points>, bold = TRUE/FALSE), and gap (list(size = ): the blank line below the title). A list is merged over the built-in values key by key, so list(entry = list(size = 9)) changes the entries' size only. Built in: title 14 pt bold, heading 11 pt bold, entry 10 pt, gap 9 pt. A size is a positive number of points, whole or half (10.5). entry also takes hanging: FALSE (default) writes each entry's wrapped lines at the indent of its first line; TRUE lines them up where the title starts, after the number (see Table of Contents), and a positive whole number of twips hangs them that far in, the label written whole (list(entry = list(hanging = 360))). Headings are not affected. Default getOption("rtfreporter.toc_style"). The font is the document's (that of the first input file). Another key, a size that is not a positive number, a bold that is not TRUE / FALSE or a hanging that is not TRUE / FALSE / a positive whole number is an error.

Value

Invisibly returns output_file.

Details

Page-number fields work correctly across the assembled document provided the header/footer text uses dynamic tokens:

  • {AUTO_PAGE} – per-page number rendered by the RTF viewer, counted from the assembled file's first page.

  • {AUTO_TOTAL_PAGES} – the assembled file's total page count, a cover and the table of contents included.

See Page numbering below.

Static tokens ({TOTAL_PAGES}) reflect only the page count of the individual source file and will be wrong in the assembled output.

Cover page

Pass cover = list(...) to add a cover page section before the TOC. Recognised fields:

title

large centred bold heading (default font size 22 pt).

subtitle

medium centred line below the title (14 pt).

date

centred line (11 pt).

version

centred line (11 pt).

meta

character vector of extra centred lines (10 pt).

Any field that is NULL, NA or empty is skipped, as is an NA line of meta. Another field name, or a cover that is not a list, is an error.

Table of Contents

toc can take any of these shapes:

NULL (default)

no TOC, no bookmarks. Byte-for-byte the pre-v0.0.29 behaviour.

"auto"

each input file's title as a level-1 TOC entry. The title is the file's title rows (the centred bold rows rtf_titles() writes at the top of the body), read as the file shows them and joined into one entry with two spaces between them ("Table 1" and "Demographics" give "Table 1 Demographics"); a line break inside a row ("\n") is joined the same way, never printed as \line. A table, a figure and a listing are each labelled by their title; a file with no title rows takes its running header's "Table N" line ("Table 14.1.1 Demographic Characteristics": the title written after the number on that line, whatever centred lines follow it, a population line for one; a line with the number only takes the longest other centred line that is not a <...> subtitle), and a file with neither, its file name without .rtf. A file gets one entry however many pages it has: a file whose titles change from page to page ("Summary of {PARAM}" with page_by) is labelled by its first page's title. Its tokens are filled ({STUDY}, {PAGE}), except that a dynamic page number ({AUTO_PAGE}, {AUTO_TOTAL_PAGES}) and the {BOOK_PAGE} slot are left out, and markup keeps its text without its formatting. assemble_folder() labels its rows the same way.

a character vector of TOC labels

one per input file – same as "auto" but with explicit labels.

a table (data.frame)

one row per file, in order, for multi-level (chapter / table) layouts: file (the path), and optionally label (the entry text; a row with no label, or an NA one, takes its file's title, read as "auto" reads it), heading (a heading printed above the row's entry whenever it changes; NA = none), level (the entry's indent, a whole number from 1 to 3, default 2) and order. assemble_folder() makes one from a folder, ready to edit. input_files can then be left out: the table's file column is used.

the path of such a table

an .xlsx or .csv file, e.g. the one assemble_folder(spec_file = ) wrote and you edited.

Each TOC entry is an RTF HYPERLINK field; clicking it in Word / Pages jumps to a per-source-file bookmark. Each row also has a PAGEREF field so the page number next to the entry is calculated by the viewer when the file opens.

The page number stands on a right tab at the right margin. A label too long for one line wraps before the page-number column, never into it: each entry has a right indent (\ri) of the column's width plus a gap, six characters at the entry's font size (four digits and two spaces; more when a page number has more digits), 720 twips (0.5 in) at the default 10 pt. The page number and its leader stay on the label's last line, at the margin. Every level has it, with or without a hanging indent; headings do not. An entry is also kept on one page (\keep): Word never splits it across two TOC pages.

With a hanging indent (toc_style = list(entry = list(hanging = TRUE))) an entry is its number, a tab and its title ("Table 14.3.2", then "Summary of ..."), and the title's wrapped lines start where its first line does, after the number. The hang is the width of the widest number in the TOC and a gap of 1 em at the entry's size: a character is 0.6 em in Courier New (exact) and is taken as 0.75 em in any other font (a generous estimate: a wrong one leaves a little too much room). Two more tab stops follow the hang, 2 and 4 em after it, so a number wider than the hang puts its title at the next of them, never at the page number's tab. With "auto" and assemble_folder() the number is the one the file's title is read with ("Table 14.1.1"); a label given as text is split when it starts with Table, Figure or Listing and a number (14.3.2, 14.3.2.1, 14.1.1a). A label that does not split is written whole, its wrapped lines at the same hang; when no label splits the hang is 720 twips. A whole number of twips (hanging = 360) is the hang as given, and each label is written whole, its wrapped lines that far in.

Page numbering

Every page of the assembled file is numbered in one Arabic sequence from its first page, and the total is the count of all its pages. The cover, when there is one, is page 1; the table of contents' pages come next, then the input files' pages, with no restart anywhere. With a cover, a one-page table of contents and 7 pages of tables, the pages read 1 of 9 (the cover), 2 of 9 (the table of contents), 3 of 9 (the first table) ... 9 of 9; without the cover, 1 of 8 (the table of contents), 2 of 8 (the first table) ... 8 of 8.

The inputs' {AUTO_PAGE} / {AUTO_TOTAL_PAGES}, the book_page text and the page numbers the table of contents shows all follow this sequence. The file is written with the total already in place (every NUMPAGES field's cached value is the count of all pages) and with each table of contents entry's cached page number, so a viewer that does not refresh fields shows them too.

Examples

# two TFL files in a folder, as a study's output
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "tfl")
dir.create(dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
for (t in c("14.1.1", "14.2.1")) {
  doc <- rtf_document() |>
    rtf_tables(data.frame(Parameter = "Age", Value = "75.1")) |>
    rtf_titles(list(c(paste("Table", t), "Safety Population")))
  generate_rtfreport(doc, file.path(dir, paste0("t", gsub(".", "_", t,
    fixed = TRUE), ".rtf")), overwrite = TRUE)
}
a <- file.path(dir, "t14_1_1.rtf")
b <- file.path(dir, "t14_2_1.rtf")
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".rtf")

# Plain concatenation (legacy behaviour)
assemble_rtf(c(a, b), out, overwrite = TRUE)

# Auto-TOC: one entry per file, label extracted from each title
assemble_rtf(c(a, b), out, toc = "auto", overwrite = TRUE)

# Multi-level TOC with section headings + cover page (pages 1, 2, 3, 4)
assemble_rtf(
  input_files = c(a, b),
  output_file = out,
  cover = list(
    title    = "Study XYZ-001",
    subtitle = "Final Statistical Report",
    date     = "2026-05-28",
    version  = "v1.0",
    meta     = c("Confidential", "Prepared by ACME Pharma")
  ),
  toc = data.frame(
    file    = c(a, b),
    heading = c("DEMOGRAPHICS", "SAFETY ANALYSES"),
    label   = c("Table 14.1.1 Demographics", "Table 14.2.1 Adverse Events")
  ),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
